title: What is known about 1RB0RE_1LC0RA_1RF0RD_---1LE_0LB1LE_1LE1RC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RE_1LC0RA_1RF0RD_---1LE_0LB1LE_1LE1RC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Open. The run is a bouncer inside a bouncer: an inner tape 1x(10)y11 is swept linearly, its resets double it, and each inner reset takes a slowly growing amount (12, 13, 14, 15, 16, …) from an outer block (10)C with C = 32,751 at 5·109 steps. The outer counter will last about 250 inner resets, so the next outer event is about 2250 steps away. Lean proves that any halt happens at the right edge of the tape (state D reading blank tape).

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (D0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 32,789 cells have been visited and 26,426 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.266). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.415).

claims.title: Halting only at the right edge
claims.text: A closed tape language of windows of 4 cells covers the whole run from blank tape; in it the halting transition D0 fires only with blank tape from the head onward. So the machine halts iff state D reaches the blank region to the right.

claims.title: The sweep rules
claims.text: Three one-sweep rules found and proved by bbtools.cycles: one sweep turns one 11 pair into two 10 pairs, for all sizes (with and without the outer context).

claims.title: Which resets halt
claims.text: Started on otherwise blank tape from (10)y 11 (head in B on the last cell), the machine halts for y = 2j − j − 5 (j = 4..11: 7, 22, 53, 116, 243, 498, 1009, 2032) and y = 12, and for no other y < 2500 within 3y² + 105 steps. (That the whole family 2j − j − 5 halts is now a Lean theorem, below.)

claims.title: The two levels
claims.text: At the moments B is at the right end the tape is 1<sup>10</sup>(10)<sup>C</sup>1<sup>x</sup>(10)<sup>y</sup>11 (after 5·10<sup>9</sup> steps). Sweeps move x → x−2, y → y+2; inner resets roughly double x+y and lower C by 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, … (one more each time). Read off the run up to 2·10<sup>10</sup> steps.

claims.title: The doubling rounds
claims.text: With P(x, y) = 0 1x 0 (10)y 1 B> and D(m, c) = C> 0 (10)m 1c at the left end: the sweep P(x+2, y) → P(x, y+2) whatever lies to the left; a top-level empty tank P(1, y+2) (blank tape to the left) reaches D(1, 2y+12); and one round D(m, c+2m+6) → D(2m+3, c+2) for all m, c and tapes to the right (left block 1, 5, 13, 29, 61, …), any number of rounds by induction. Leaf rules by bbtools.symtm.prove.

claims.title: The halting resets, for every j
claims.text: A top-level reset from (10)y+1 1 B> (the tank (10)y 11 two steps later) on blank tape halts whenever y = 2j − j − 5, j ≥ 4: after j − 2 rounds exactly two 1s are left, and D reaches blank tape.

claims.title: How a top-level reset ends
claims.text: With K(C, y) = (10)C 0 (10)y 1 B> (an inner empty tank): a doubling round D(q+j+1, 2j+6) on blank tape, too short for a full round, leaves 2q+1 ones on the left as the outer stock and reaches K(2j, 7) to their right, the outer block being (10)2j (round_end, through top_end: 1^(p+1) B> 1 0 (10)^(i+2) 1 1 → 1^(p+1) 0 (10)^i 0 (10)^7 1 B>). This is how the second level starts.

claims.title: The inner reset map
claims.text: For every C, y and every tape on the left: an inner tank K(C+2, y) turns into 2y+7 ones and uses two outer pairs (g_entry); then inner rounds run, each using one more outer pair and doubling its block, k → 2k+6 (6, 18, 42, 90, …; g_step, g_end); when the rounds run out with one 1 on the right a new inner bouncer starts and sweeps to the next tank (g_term, p_sweeps). inner_reset: innerMap C y = some (C′, y′) implies K(C, y) reaches K(C′, y′), with innerMap an explicit Lean function. It is none only when the outer block is too short (an outer event) or a round starts with exactly three 1s on the right (further nesting); those cases are not covered.

claims.title: The top-level tanks 8187 and 16379, followed
claims.text: From the top-level empty tank y = 16,379 of the run (blank tape on the left): 12 doubling rounds, the outer stock 132,737, the outer block (10)24, then inner tanks y = 7, 19, 43, 91, 187 with outer blocks 24, 20, 15, 9, 2 (tank_16379). From y = 8187: 11 rounds, stock 116,355, inner tanks 7, 19, 43, 91 with outer blocks 22, 18, 13, 7 (tank_8187). The outer block drops by 4, 5, 6, 7: two pairs for the entry and one per inner round. That the run reaches these tanks is not in Lean (the README’s plain runs).

claims.title: The near misses
claims.text: By the same count, the tanks y = 2<sup>j</sup> − 5 of the run from blank tape leave 2j + 2 ones after j − 2 rounds instead of 2; the leftover becomes the second-level structure. Why the run keeps landing on 2<sup>j</sup> − 5 is not explained.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known; the next outer event is about 2250 steps away. The end of a top-level reset and the inner reset of the second level are now theorems (lean/Level2.lean); not yet in Lean: the outer event (an inner round that finds the outer block used up, which hands the run back to a top-level bouncer), the rare inner round that starts with exactly three 1s, and hence the full two-level map.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows: the machine runs a bouncer inside a bouncer, and the outer one will not move again for about 2<sup>250</sup> steps.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 32,789 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
Any halt happens with blank tape from the head on (Lean).
Inner bouncer doubles per reset; an outer counter pays for each reset.
Every top-level reset from such a y halts: proved in Lean for all j.
The inner reset of the second level is a Lean function, proved for all sizes.

sections.heading: The inner bouncer
html: Each time the head is at the right end in state B the right part of the tape is 1x (10)y 11, and one sweep takes two 1s and makes two 10 pairs, exactly as in 1RB0RB_1LC0LF_1RD0LB_1RE1RC_0RA---_1LA1RE:
When the 1s run out the block of 10s is turned back into a block of 1s about twice as long (16,379 pairs become 132,736), and the sweeps start again.

The reset is a run of doubling rounds: at the left end, a block of m pairs 10 becomes a block of 2m+3 pairs (1, 5, 13, 29, 61, …), and each round eats 2m+4 of the 1s. The sweep, the start of a reset and the rounds are Lean theorems for all sizes (p_sweeps, top_reset, rounds).

sections.heading: A counter that pays for each reset
html: From about 5·109 steps on, the inner bouncer sits to the right of a block (10)C, and each inner reset takes a little of it:

C drops by 13, 14, 15, 16 (one more at each reset, about the number of doubling rounds of the reset) while the inner part doubles. With C = 32,751 to spend, the outer block lasts about 250 inner resets: the inner part will be about 2250 cells wide before anything new happens. Earlier in the run the same thing happened at smaller scale (outer blocks of 64 and 13 pairs ran out after a few inner resets).

sections.heading: The inner reset as a function
html: When the doubling rounds of a top-level reset run short, the 1s left over stay on the left as the outer stock, the pairs become the outer block, and a small bouncer starts to their right: 1^(2q+1) 0 (10)^(2j) 0 (10)^7 1 B> (round_end). An inner reset from an empty tank (10)^C 0 (10)^y 1 B> then runs the same doubling rounds, except that each round takes one pair from the outer block:

(10)^28 0 A> 0 1^87                 entry: y = 40, two outer pairs used
(10)^27 1^6 0 A> 0 1^83             round 1 (one pair used)
(10)^26 1^18 0 A> 0 1^73            round 2, block 6 -> 18
(10)^25 1^42 0 A> 0 1^51            round 3, 18 -> 42
(10)^24 1^90 0 A> 0 1^5             round 4, 42 -> 90

When the 1s on the right run out, a new inner bouncer sweeps to the next empty tank. Lean proves every piece for all sizes and any tape to the left, and the whole inner reset as one function innerMap (inner_reset). From the run’s top-level tank y = 16,379 Lean follows the reset into the second level and through four inner resets: tanks 7, 19, 43, 91, 187, outer block 24, 20, 15, 9, 2. What is not in Lean yet is the outer event, when a round finds the outer block used up.

sections.heading: What halting would require
html: Lean proves (from a closed tape language, kernel-checked) that the machine can only halt in state D on blank tape at the right edge. Counting the doubling rounds shows when that happens at a top-level reset: if exactly two 1s are left at the start of a round, D runs off the tape. That is the case exactly for y = 2j − j − 5 (7, 22, 53, 116, 243, …), and this is now a Lean theorem for every j (reset_halts). The run from blank tape reached top-level resets with y = 8187 = 213 − 5 and y = 16379 = 214 − 5: by the same count they leave 2j + 2 ones instead of 2, a near miss by exactly j. Whether a halt ever happens is open, and the next outer reset is far beyond any simulation.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.266). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.415).
After 109 steps the tape spans 32,789 cells (130 left of the start, 20,991 right), with a density of 1s of 0.806.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Bouncer 1^x (10)^y 11 trading 1s for 10s, nested inside a second level: each reset of the inner bouncer doubles it and takes about log2(size) from an outer counter (10)^C; can halt only at the right edge (Lean).
